1.referenceTitle: NHC/SAMR Announcement No. 6 of 2025 publishing GB 2762-2025
1.citation: National Health Commission and State Administration for Market Regulation, China. Announcement No. 6 of 2025, publishing GB 2762-2025 and other national food-safety standards. Dated September 2, 2025; posted September 25, 2025. Supplemented by USDA FAS report CH2025-0202.
1.summary: The announcement formally publishes GB 2762-2025 among 32 standards and two amendments. The accompanying USDA translation identifies September 2, 2026 as the replacement standard’s effective date.
1.establishes: The announcement verifies adoption and identity; it does not print the effective date or numerical tables in its HTML. The reviewed translation is expressly unofficial. The 2025 standard is effective by this review date.
1.relevance: HMTc’s China comparison should now identify the 2025 edition and match its product rows. A publication notice alone cannot establish that a certification threshold meets each Chinese requirement.

links.label: NHC/SAMR Announcement No. 6 of 2025 publishing GB 2762-2025

evidence.note: Read title, publication metadata, announcement body and signed date. The HTML directs readers to the official standards platform but contains no effective-date statement. Distinguish the September 2 issue date from September 25 web publication.

Reused same-day exact-document review in batch4-four-eight.json ref 6: report highlights, replacement foreword and relevant standard sections. USDA identifies September 2, 2026 implementation and replacement of GB 2762-2022 plus its first amendment; this is an unofficial translation, not a claim of direct access to the authoritative Chinese tables.

2.referenceTitle: Heavy Metal Index — China GB 2762 contaminants
2.citation: Pendergrass K / Institute of Contaminant Standards. China GB 2762-2022—Maximum levels of contaminants in food. Heavy Metal Index. Updated May 18, 2026.
2.summary: This index page describes the 2022 standard and records its planned replacement by GB 2762-2025 on September 2, 2026. Its active-status language is expressly dated May 18, 2026.
2.establishes: It is a secondary instrument record, not a Chinese government standard. Its historical date qualification must be preserved: an active label for the 2022 edition is stale after the replacement date.
2.relevance: It provides a source trail for HMTc’s market file. The current comparison needs the effective successor and cannot rely on this older status label as proof of present compliance.

links.label: Heavy Metal Index — China GB 2762 contaminants

evidence.note: Read overview, scope, HMT&C interaction, sources, verification notes, update metadata and operator footer. It says scheduled replacement is after the current session date, meaning its May snapshot; today is September 15, 2026. The page links older official/USDA records but does not display the successor standard artifact claimed in the article. Operator is ICS/Paleo Certified, so this is not an independent regulator.

3.citation: National Health Commission, China. Public consultation register (征求意见). Register accessed September 15, 2026.
3.summary: The register lists dated consultations, including a June 15, 2026 food-safety standards work plan and an April 17, 2026 package of 37 draft food-safety standards.
3.establishes: It demonstrates a standards-development pipeline. A register entry does not establish adoption, an effective date, a particular proposed metal concentration, or that comments remain open today.
3.relevance: It is a monitoring source for HMTc’s China market file. Any proposed product limit needs its own attachment and status review before becoming a specification.

evidence.note: Read the complete visible first-page register, including dated 2026 and older entries. Web reader returned 412, but direct HTML retrieval succeeded. No consultation attachment was reviewed or used to assert a numerical contaminant change.

4.citation: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, Republic of Korea. Partial amendment to Food Standards and Specifications, Notice 2025-56, August 26, 2025.
4.summary: The official notice identifies new cadmium criteria for cocoa powder and chocolate among broader food-code amendments. It gives the amendment number and adoption date and links the underlying HWPX files.
4.establishes: The visible notice supports the existence and stated subject of the amendment. Its summary does not supply the complete numerical tiers or their commencement provisions.
4.relevance: It justifies checking the applicable Korean cocoa or chocolate row in HMTc’s market file. A cataloged amendment is not itself a completed product-level compliance comparison.

evidence.note: Read Korean notice title, metadata, reasons and major changes, especially item 2(b) establishing cocoa/chocolate cadmium criteria, and the attachment list. The attached HWPX text was not inspected; no numerical maximum, uniform commencement date or exhaustive current Food Code claim is made here.

5.citation: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration. Method of Test for Heavy Metals in Edible Fat, Oil, Cream, Chocolate and Cocoa Powder. MOHWH0029.01, amended January 1, 2026. Six-page English method.
5.summary: The method uses microwave acid digestion and ICP-MS for arsenic, mercury and lead in edible fats, oils and cream, and cadmium in chocolate and cocoa powder. It specifies preparation, calibration, blanks and quantification.
5.establishes: Its quantification limits are 0.025 mg/kg for the named elements in fats/oils/cream and 0.02 mg/kg for cocoa/chocolate cadmium. These analytical capabilities are not legal contaminant maxima or arsenic-speciation results.
5.relevance: It helps match an HMTc laboratory evidence package to the relevant Taiwanese food matrix and analyte. It does not impose this method on every food or prove acceptance of any certificate.

evidence.note: Downloaded and read all six pages: identity and scope, digestion and ICP-MS procedures, calculation and final remarks requiring validation where interference occurs or alternative instruments are used. The article’s generic multi-element wording should retain these specific food/analyte restrictions; the method is not an all-food or inorganic-arsenic method.

6.referenceTitle: Hong Kong CFS metallic-contamination amendment hub
6.citation: Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety. Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) (Amendment) Regulation 2025: official implementation hub.
6.summary: The hub states that the amendment began on September 5, 2025. During an 18-month grace period, any food may comply wholly with either the prior Cap. 132V requirements or the amendment; all food must meet the amendment from March 6, 2027.
6.establishes: The grace period is an alternative complete-regime compliance provision. The hub also links the legal instrument, guidelines and testing presentations; those linked tables were not all reviewed here.
6.relevance: HMTc’s Hong Kong comparison needs both the relevant schedule and transition status. The article’s restriction of the grace period to pre-existing foods is narrower than the official explanation.

links.label: Hong Kong CFS metallic-contamination amendment hub

evidence.note: Read the full hub, particularly introduction paragraphs on July 30 legislative approval, September 5 commencement and the March 6, 2027 deadline. The text explicitly says any food item may comply wholly with either regime; it does not limit this option to stock already present before commencement. No current individual product limit is inferred from the hub alone.

7.citation: GCC Standardization Organization. GSO 2783:2025, Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) for Heavy Metals in Food. Gulf Technical Regulation, edition 1; catalog approval date October 29, 2025. Public catalog record.
7.summary: The catalog identifies a current 22-page English technical regulation covering arsenic, inorganic arsenic, mercury, cadmium, lead and tin in food.
7.establishes: The reviewed scope and edition metadata do not expose the licensed numerical tables or establish a common implementation date in every GCC member state. The displayed date is approval, not a verified national effective date.
7.relevance: It is a starting point for HMTc’s Gulf market file. A member-state legal review and the applicable licensed product table are still needed before claiming market access.

evidence.note: Read the directly retrieved official catalog in full: current edition, approval date, page count and scope. Web reader failed but local HTML succeeded. Paid contents were not accessed. Scope names six analyte categories; no inference of universal GCC adoption or all-food limits is made.

8.citation: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Amendment Regulations, 2026. Notification F. No. 01/SP-02/S&S/NotificationContaminants/2021-22, May 14, 2026. Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III, Section 4, No. 327; CG-DL-E-25052026-272840. Effective December 1, 2026.
8.summary: The final amendment extends lead and cadmium pulse categories to pulse flours. For fish oils it applies an inorganic-arsenic maximum of 0.1 mg/kg: total arsenic below that value clears the screen; a value above it requires inorganic-arsenic testing.
8.establishes: The amendment is adopted but takes effect December 1, 2026. The pulse changes expand product scope rather than publishing new numerical pulse limits. Total arsenic is a screen, not the regulated fish-oil species.
8.relevance: It gives HMTc a fixed India readiness date and a specific laboratory decision sequence. Product classification and applicable base-regulation limits still matter; certification alone does not establish market access.

evidence.note: Retrieved the exact six-page government Gazette and read English notification and amendments on pp. 4–6, plus first-page identity. Notification is May 14; printed Gazette masthead is May 19, while document identifier, digital signature and register posting use May 25. Keep these dates distinct. §1(2) fixes December 1, 2026 effect; §2 gives pulse-flour substitutions and the fish-oil screening note. No rule is supplied for exact equality in the screening note.

The complete indexed official register excerpt was read and lists Amendment 17 as May 25, 2026. Direct old-host retrieval timed out; the original www register returned a JavaScript shell. The substantive explanation therefore rests on the exact final government Gazette, not the index or secondary summaries.

9.citation: Ministry of Health, Vietnam. Circular 12/2024/TT-BYT of July 18, 2024, promulgating QCVN 20-1:2024/BYT on contaminant limits in health supplements/dietary supplements. Official Gazette 895–896, August 5, 2024; effective August 1, 2025.
9.summary: Table 1 sets total arsenic 5, inorganic arsenic 1.5, lead 10 and mercury 0.5 mg/kg or mg/L. Cadmium is 3 for supplements containing seaweed or bivalve ingredients and 1 otherwise. Inorganic arsenic is checked when total arsenic exceeds 1.5.
9.establishes: The binding supplement rule includes product scope, transition terms and a conditional cadmium tier. Registered products made before commencement can continue to expiry under stated conditions; this is not a limit for every food.
9.relevance: It supplies a concrete Vietnamese comparator for HMTc supplement specifications. Claims that all mapped HMTc cells are stricter require a separate review of those cells, species and mass-versus-volume bases.

evidence.note: Read official Gazette index metadata identifying enactment July 18, 2024 and effect August 1, 2025; followed its PDF link.

Read Circular Articles 1–5 on PDF pp. 1–2, QCVN scope on p. 5 and Table 1 on p. 6 (Gazette pp. 2–3, 6–7). Excludes tonic wine declared as a health supplement. Transition covers registered products manufactured before effect and pending applications. The cadmium 3 mg/kg or mg/L tier applies to products containing the stated ingredients without an 80% threshold. No HMTc table comparison was independently validated from this legal source.

10.referenceTitle: UK Government: SPS agreement, preparing your business
10.citation: UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs. SPS agreement: preparing your business. Guidance updated July 30, 2026.
10.summary: The guidance describes planned UK–EU sanitary and phytosanitary arrangements, with an intended mid-2027 start. Food/feed contaminants and food-contact materials are among the negotiating areas; timing and exceptions remain subject to negotiation.
10.establishes: This is business-preparation guidance about a prospective agreement, not an adopted schedule of new contaminant limits or a guaranteed commencement date.
10.relevance: HMTc can use it to prepare UK–EU product and evidence comparisons while preserving the pending status. Certification does not substitute for the final agreement or each applicable rule.

links.label: UK Government: SPS agreement, preparing your business

evidence.note: Read update date, introductory timing paragraphs, scope and exceptions, and digital-system sections. The government says intent and ongoing negotiations. No later agreement, final exceptions or precise future contaminant obligations were assumed from this guidance.
